newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures slip in lacklustre market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures slip in lacklustre market.

text.p: Rubber futures finished marginally lower on Wednesday in listless trade with prices drifting on lack of firm buying by major consumers, dealers said.
"Offtake again was non-existent so prices were marked lower since sentiment was so weak. It may continue drifting tomorrow unless fresh buying picks up the market," a local rubber trader said.
Slightly higher Tokyo prices, with benchmark February inching up 0.3 yen to 140.3, failed to lift the market, dealers said.
"We had another quiet session, nothing extraordinary. The volumes were very light," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 128.00 U.S. cents a kg from 128.50 cents.
November RSS1 was seen at 183.50-184.50 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.31) a kg from Tuesday's settlement of 184.50 cents.
November TSR20 was seen at 178.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg against the previous 178.50 cents.
